maria_p: Heads-up — FinSimplify asked for a hard burst guarantee across eu-west and us-central for their reserved pool. They want an approach that avoids double-booking and ensures fast handoff to autoscale slots. Need product + eng tradeoffs and a launchable plan by EOW.

samir_eng: Can you share the specific SLO they're asking for? hard guarantee means we may need pre-reserved warm slots or deterministic spillover.

maria_p: They proposed 99.9% for <=150ms p95 on baseline plus 30k token bursts per minute for up to 10 minutes, twice per day. They want contract language that says "burstable without preemption" within the region.

jo_cse: That's high. From onboarding notes: FinSimplify will take 3x our average seq length and has lots of short chats — pattern is spiky. They'll pay for a premium add-on but expect playbook and runbook.

alex_sales: Commercially doable if we offer a bundling: reserved core + burst slots + SLA uplift. Price it as "Burst Guarantee Add-on". Need ops to confirm feasibility.

samir_eng: Technical options:
- Option A: Sync reserve slots across regions (reservation window + slot pinning). Fast handoff: route to pinned slot then fallback to autoscale.
- Option B: Dedicated warm pool for customer with strict pre-provisioning (higher cost but simple).
- Option C: Soft-burst with admission control + best-effort failover (cheaper, weaker promise).

diane_sre: Risk notes: Option A complexity: cross-region coordination, clock skew can cause 1-2s mismatch — acceptable? Option B increases utilization overhead ~20-30% but deterministic. Monitoring/alerts will need new signals (slot saturation, handoff latency).

maria_p: For go/no-go we need: launch criteria, expected incremental cost, changes to SLA wording, and a minimal ops playbook. Can we prototype Option A as MVP? Prefer lower run rate than full dedicated warm pool.

samir_eng: MVP sketch for Option A: reserve-slot-synchronization (RSS) service that does three things:
1) Reservation ledger per-customer per-region
2) Atomic handoff API for router to claim a slot
3) Fail-open policy -> if claim fails after X ms, route to autoscale variant and mark incident for billing adjust
Sample policy YAML:```yaml
reserve_policy:
  customer: finsimplify
  regions: [eu-west, us-central]
  burst_window_minutes: 10
  daily_burst_allowance: 2
  max_concurrent_slots: 50
  claim_timeout_ms: 200
  fallback: autoscale_variant
```
This keeps the router logic minimal.

jo_cse: Claim timeout 200ms is aggressive but matches customer latency ask. If claim fails we must surface transparent reason in console. Also need a billing marker when fallback engages.

diane_sre: Observability additions: new metrics: `reserve_claim_latency_ms`, `reserve_claim_failure{reason}`, `reserve_utilization_pct`. We'll want alerting: >90% utilization for 5m and claim_failure_rate>1% for 10m. Also an automated mitigation runbook: prewarm additional slots if utilization trending up.

alex_sales: Contract language suggestion: "Burst Guarantee Add-on: Redwood will maintain reserved burst capacity (as defined in policy) with claim-time handoff. In periods where reserved claims cannot be honored due to force-majeure (regional outage or hardware failure), Redwood will route to an autoscale variant and credit the customer for unmet burst minutes." Need legal to approve.

maria_p: Can eng give an estimate for MVP effort and perf risk? Prioritize: correct accounting > 95th latency target > autoscale fallback behavior.

samir_eng: Rough estimates:
- RSS service + router API: 3 engineer-weeks (core) + 1 week for infra hardening
- Router integration + canary: 2 eng-weeks
- Observability + alerts: 1 eng-week
- Billing markers + console UI: 1.5 eng-weeks (we'll need product/design)
Total ~8-9 engineer-weeks across squads. Perf risk low if claim path stays <200ms. Biggest unknown: cross-region ledger consistency under load.

jo_cse: For launch we should require a pilot with one customer (FinSimplify) and internal load tests that simulate 3x seq length and spike patterns. Also acceptance criteria:
- Sustained claim_latency_p95 < 200ms under pilot traffic
- Fallback correctness (no double-alloc) verified in chaos tests
- Billing markers accurate for every fallback event
- Runbook validated with oncall drill

maria_p: Good. Prioritization ask: move this into Q2 roadmap as a pilot item. Blockers: legal SLA wording, billing export changes, and infra capacity for prewarm. Who owns the pilot?

samir_eng: Eng runtime team will own the RSS service (samir + taylor). Router team will own router changes (diane + rachel). Observability handled by eng-infra.

diane_sre: I'll add the runbook and schedule a tabletop once we have initial metrics. Recommend an early canary to internal beta org first.

alex_sales: I'll align commercial terms with FinSimplify and loop legal. Expect negotiation on credits; propose 1.5x credits per unmet minute as compromise.

maria_p: OK action items:
- samir: make a short RFC draft with the YAML and failure semantics by Tue EOD
- diane: runbook skeleton + initial alert thresholds by Wed
- jo: pilot test plan + acceptance checklist by Thu
- alex: term sheet draft + pricing sketch by Fri
We'll reconvene Friday to finalize launch criteria. :white_check_mark:

autoscale-bot: Deploy plan created: `deploy rfc/3298765432-rss-mvp` (status: draft)

samir_eng: Added initial RFC link in #rfc (will ping when ready). Thanks all.

maria_p: Thanks team — keeping scope narrow for pilot. We'll decide whether to expand to dedicated warm pool after pilot based on utilization delta. :rocket:
